newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Soccer-Ireland will not take Macedonia for granted.
newsitem.headline: Soccer-Ireland will not take Macedonia for granted.

text.p: Republic of Ireland manager Mick McCarthy said that his players would not take Macedonia for granted when the sides meet in a World Cup Group Eight qualifier at Lansdowne Road on Wednesday.
"Just look at the results with Armenia drawing against Northern Ireland in Belfast and then the Ukraine beating Portugal. That should be a warning to us as we approach the game," McCarthy said.

"I have had reports on the Macedonians and watched a video of their 1-1 draw with Iceland earlier in the tournament. They work very hard and they will be difficult to beat. We won't underestimate them," he added.

Macedonia, who only came into being as a competitive footballing nation in the last European Championship qualifying competition, beat Liechtenstein 3-0 in their opening game and top Group Eight ahead of their visit to Ireland.
They have arrived in Dublin without former Red Star Belgrade and Inter Milan striker Darko Pancev and the highly-regarded midfielder Mitko Stojkovski, both of whom are injured.
But in defenders Sasa Nikoloski and Goce Sedloski and striker Gorgi Hristov, Macedonia have proven talent at their disposal.
"I can be honest and say we have very talented players. Maybe not so experienced but they are players with potential," team coach Dokica Hadzievski said.

"It's very difficult to say we have a big chance against Ireland. Nobody can play and think about losing. We have to be positive and have strong hope and motivation in the match," the former CSKA Sofia coach added.
Ireland defeated Liechtenstein 5-0 on August 31 in their only outing in the World Cup qualifying rounds to date.

Liechtenstein held Ireland to a scoreless draw on the previous occasion that the sides met in a European Championship qualifier in 1995, a result which ultimately cost the Irish a place in the finals in England.
That result has taught Ireland how costly it can be to underestimate the opposition at international level.
McCarthy has had to plan without experienced international midfielders Ray Houghton and Roy Keane as well as striker Niall Quinn for Wednesday's clash which kicks off at 1930 local time.

Aston Villa's Steve Staunton is expected to move from defence to join Andy Townsend and Alan McLoughlin in the centre of midfield with Jason McAteer and Ian Harte filling the wide roles in a 3-5-2 formation.
Denis Irwin, Gary Breen and Phil Babb are likely to make up the last line of defence in front of goalkeeper Shay Given.

Dubliner Keith O'Neill, scorer of four goals in seven games for Ireland, and veteran John Aldridge are favourites to start up front. Aldridge, 38, needs only one more international goal to equal Frank Stapleton's record of 20 international strikes.
IRELAND (probable): Shay Given; Denis Irwin, Gary Breen, Phil Babb; Jason McAteer, Alan McLoughlin, Steve Staunton, Andy Townsend, Ian Harte; Keith O'Neill, John Aldridge.
